subject: math
name: fostering classroom belonging
problemType: students feel isolated or excluded during math collaboration.
targetMisconception: belief that belonging is unrelated to academic success.
teacherMoves: establish norms of mutual respect (udl 8.3)
facilitate cooperative structures ensuring all voices (hlp cooperative learning)
conduct regular community-building check-ins (udl 9.3)
studentTasks: engage in rotating partner or group tasks.
contribute at least one idea per discussion.
fadePlan: teacher leads community routines. • gradually delegate role assignment to students. • fade as culture becomes self-sustaining.
whenNotToUse: avoid when addressing confidential or individual assessment feedback.
formativeChecks: - peer feedback on group climate. - teacher observation logs.

subject: math
name: collaborative resilience circles
problemType: groups falter after initial failure on challenging tasks.
targetMisconception: belief that peers cannot help when stuck.
teacherMoves: facilitate quick reflection huddles mid-task (udl 8.3)
provide structure for collective problem-solving (hlp cooperative learning)
model language for requesting help (udl 2.1)
studentTasks: share what was tried and what next.
supports: resilience circle protocol card (hlp cooperative learning)
fadePlan: teacher initiates structured huddles. • students later self-initiate check-ins without card prompts.
whenNotToUse: avoid with very short activities lacking collaboration.
formativeChecks: - observation rubric of group persistence. - student self-rating of collaboration.

subject: math
name: academic goal-setting and reflection
problemType: students lack ownership of learning targets.
targetMisconception: belief that grades are outside of personal control.
teacherMoves: model setting smart math goals (udl 6.4)
confer individually to refine measurable criteria (hlp feedback)
celebrate incremental progress (udl 9.1)
studentTasks: draft and track personal math goals.
fadePlan: teacher models and monitors initial goals. • reduce scaffolds as students self-track and adjust independently.
whenNotToUse: avoid when class is completing externally-scored standardized testing.
formativeChecks: - review goal trackers biweekly. - reflection conference notes.

subject: math
name: growth-mindset language and feedback
problemType: students express fixed beliefs about math ability.
targetMisconception: belief that intelligence is static and success means innate talent.
teacherMoves: use process-focused feedback (udl 8.1)
share brain plasticity mini-lessons (hlp motivation)
model vulnerability discussing own struggles (udl 7.3)
studentTasks: write reflection on one mistake that led to growth.
fadePlan: teacher models language first. • students practice with prompts. • fade supports as positive self-talk becomes habitual.
whenNotToUse: avoid when time is needed for procedural fluency practice only.
formativeChecks: - collect language samples pre/post. - student self-rating of confidence.

subject: math
name: reducing math anxiety through predictable routines
problemType: students freeze or avoid participation in math due to anxiety.
targetMisconception: belief that mistakes in math are proof of low ability.
teacherMoves: establish consistent warm-up routine with low-stakes entry (udl 7.2)
model self-talk reframing errors as data (hlp social/emotional support)
provide calm feedback emphasizing progress (udl 9.1)
studentTasks: reflect on effort rather than correctness.
share one learning gain per week.
fadePlan: teacher leads structured warm-ups and reflection prompts. • gradually shorten teacher cueing as students internalize routine.
whenNotToUse: avoid during summative test preparation windows requiring timed pacing.
formativeChecks: - student self-report on anxiety levels. - teacher notes of participation change.

subject: math
name: building positive math identity
problemType: students do not see themselves as 'math people'.
targetMisconception: belief that math identity belongs only to high achievers.
teacherMoves: display diverse mathematician stories (udl 7.3)
invite students to connect math to personal interests (hlp relevance)
use reflective journaling on math self-concept (udl 6.4)
studentTasks: write connection between math and own life.
fadePlan: begin with structured biography prompts. • shift to student-selected role models and self-connections.
whenNotToUse: avoid when lesson time is limited to procedural test prep.
formativeChecks: - review identity journals for self-concept change. - peer sharing feedback.

subject: math
name: normalizing productive struggle
problemType: students give up quickly when problems feel hard.
targetMisconception: belief that speed equals intelligence.
teacherMoves: share examples of productive struggle and recovery (udl 7.2)
model think-aloud showing perseverance (hlp modeling)
praise effort strategies explicitly (udl 8.1)
studentTasks: document thinking steps even when incomplete.
discuss what was learned from struggle.
try alternative approach before asking for help.
fadePlan: teacher models and guides reflection. • reduce prompts gradually; students self-record perseverance evidence.
whenNotToUse: avoid in timed fluency practice with fixed algorithms.
formativeChecks: - review struggle logs. - observation of persistence behaviors.

subject: math
name: connecting math to real-life relevance
problemType: students see math as disconnected from their lives.
targetMisconception: belief that math has no social or personal value.
teacherMoves: integrate culturally relevant contexts (udl 7.2)
invite students to contribute examples (hlp relevance)
facilitate discussion on societal applications (udl 8.4)
studentTasks: research real-world issues involving quantitative reasoning.
present how math can inform decisions.
fadePlan: teacher models first relevant context. • students generate own examples. • fade teacher selection; sustain student ownership.
whenNotToUse: avoid when lesson objective is isolated skill fluency only.
formativeChecks: - exit reflection: “how did this connect to your world?” - peer discussion notes.

subject: math
name: Collaborative Mathematical Problem Solving
problemType: Students solve math individually without peer collaboration benefits
targetMisconception: Belief that math is individual rather than collaborative
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical collaboration skills (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Model productive mathematical discourse (UDL 6.1)
Structure collaborative problem-solving (UDL 8.3)
Build mathematical discussion norms (UDL 8.3)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher structures collaboration with explicit roles → Phase 2: Reduced structure with collaboration norms → Phase 3: Independent collaborative work → Phase 4: Natural mathematical collaboration
whenNotToUse: When individual assessment is needed.

subject: math
name: meaning of absolute value
problemType: confusion interpreting absolute value as 'always positive' rather than distance
targetMisconception: belief that absolute value just removes negatives without meaning.
teacherMoves: model distance on number line from zero (udl 1.1)
use real-life contexts (e.g., temperature difference) (udl 7.2)
question to elicit meaning beyond sign (hlp questioning)
studentTasks: plot numbers and their distances from zero.
explain meaning of each absolute value.
fadePlan: teacher models distance examples. - students complete guided context problems. - finally, define and apply without models.
whenNotToUse: avoid during symbolic equation drills only.
formativeChecks: - verbal check: define absolute value in own words. - context matching mini-quiz.

subject: math
name: distributive property conceptual scaffold
problemType: confusion applying distributive property to expressions
targetMisconception: assuming only multiplication over addition applies in limited forms.
teacherMoves: model area representation linking to algebraic expansion (udl 3.3)
highlight common factors visually before distribution (hlp representation)
encourage verbal reasoning for each term produced (udl 6.1)
studentTasks: build algebra tiles or rectangles showing distribution.
write equivalent expressions step by step.
explain meaning of each distributed term.
fadePlan: start concrete (tiles), move to pictorial, end symbolic only. - teacher gradually withholds color and frames.
whenNotToUse: avoid during timed symbolic drills where conceptual depth isn’t goal.
formativeChecks: - spot-check tile models for accuracy. - written reflection: why distribute?

subject: math
name: equation balance and equality
problemType: misunderstanding equality as 'the answer is' instead of a relationship
targetMisconception: believing the equal sign means 'do something' not 'two sides are same value'.
teacherMoves: use balance scale model to represent equations (udl 1.1)
think-aloud maintaining balance when performing operations (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt students to check balance after each step (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: model algebraic steps with balance visuals.
write matching expressions to maintain equality.
reflect on how operations preserve equivalence.
supports: peer check protocol for equivalence (hlp peer collaboration)
fadePlan: teacher demonstrates with scale imagery. - gradually remove visuals while students justify symbolically. - final stage: students self-check without models.
whenNotToUse: avoid in pure numeric fluency drills without conceptual aim.
formativeChecks: - quick write: explain why adding to both sides keeps balance. - observation during partner checks.

subject: math
name: meaning of exponents as repeated multiplication
problemType: difficulty interpreting exponent notation conceptually
targetMisconception: thinking exponents mean multiplication by the base times the exponent.
teacherMoves: demonstrate repeated multiplication with concrete visuals (udl 3.3)
compare additive vs. multiplicative growth examples (udl 7.2)
prompt students to verbalize meaning of power notation (hlp language supports)
studentTasks: explain contrast between linear and exponential change.
supports: verbal stem cards (“___ to the power of ___ means...”) (hlp language supports)
fadePlan: teacher models first two examples with visuals. - then students complete partially filled charts. - finally, students interpret notation without aids.
whenNotToUse: avoid if class already transitioning to logarithmic operations mastery.
formativeChecks: - quick graph sketch to show difference in growth. - oral check using stem cards.

subject: math
name: understanding functions as mappings
problemType: difficulty interpreting a function as an input-output relationship
targetMisconception: thinking a function must always increase or be linear.
teacherMoves: demonstrate mapping diagrams with varied patterns (udl 3.3)
ask students to predict outputs before revealing rule (hlp questioning)
highlight non-linear examples to challenge assumption (udl 8.3)
studentTasks: match inputs and outputs using arrows or tables.
identify whether relations qualify as functions.
explain verbally what makes each relation functional.
fadePlan: start with direct teacher modeling. - move to collaborative classification. - end with independent generation of examples and counterexamples.
whenNotToUse: avoid when students are practicing advanced transformations already mastered.
formativeChecks: - quick sort of function vs. non-function cards. - oral explanation checkpoint.

subject: math
name: concept of linear relationships
problemType: misunderstanding slope as rise-over-run only without context
targetMisconception: believing slope only represents steepness, not rate of change.
teacherMoves: model real-world contexts linking rate to slope (udl 7.2)
use double-number lines to compare units (udl 1.2)
facilitate discussion connecting graph to table and context (hlp multiple representations)
studentTasks: build and interpret tables of values.
describe what slope means in context.
supports: sentence stems (“for every ___, ___ changes by ___”) (hlp multiple representations)
fadePlan: teacher leads with context-rich modeling. - gradually remove organizers as students generate interpretations independently.
whenNotToUse: avoid when working purely on symbolic slope calculations.
formativeChecks: - oral reasoning check. - quick graph-context match card.

subject: math
name: polynomial structure recognition
problemType: difficulty identifying components and hierarchy of polynomials
targetMisconception: believing polynomials are random strings of letters and numbers.
teacherMoves: highlight structure using color and grouping (udl 3.3)
compare polynomial forms through pattern sorting (hlp comparison)
model degree and term identification aloud (udl 6.1)
studentTasks: sort expressions by number of terms or degree.
fadePlan: start with modeled color-coded sorts. - gradually remove color cues and stems. - end with independent structural analysis.
whenNotToUse: avoid when students are only practicing operations fluency.
formativeChecks: - sorting observation rubric. - quick oral naming check.

subject: math
name: quadratic relationships through area models
problemType: difficulty linking quadratic equations to geometric meaning
targetMisconception: thinking squared terms are purely symbolic.
teacherMoves: use area models to show x², 2x, and constant regions (udl 3.3)
highlight symmetry visually (hlp explicit instruction)
connect to graph shape through pattern observation (udl 6.3)
fadePlan: move from physical tiles to drawn diagrams to symbolic representation. - remove templates once students justify area-based reasoning independently.
whenNotToUse: avoid when focus is factoring fluency only.
formativeChecks: - exit ticket: sketch area model and label terms.

subject: math
name: visual ratio models for proportional reasoning
problemType: difficulty connecting concrete ratio models to symbolic equations
targetMisconception: belief that proportions only exist when numbers are whole.
teacherMoves: model ratio reasoning with visual bars before symbolic notation (udl 3.3)
use a think-aloud to show unit comparison across contexts (udl 6.1)
guide students to verbalize multiplicative relationships (hlp scaffolding)
studentTasks: build and label ratio tables from visuals.
explain how one quantity changes with another.
convert a visual ratio into a proportion statement.
fadePlan: teacher fully models visual→symbol connection. - next: students complete partially filled visuals with prompts. - finally: students create and justify visuals independently.
whenNotToUse: avoid when students already show proportional reasoning fluency or when time-pressured procedural review is the goal.
formativeChecks: - observe reasoning during conversion. - exit ticket: explain a proportional relationship verbally.

subject: math
name: systems of equations across representations
problemType: struggle connecting graphical, algebraic, and contextual forms
targetMisconception: belief that each representation is unrelated.
teacherMoves: demonstrate solving same system three ways (udl 3.3)
facilitate side-by-side comparison discussion (hlp representation)
prompt students to justify equivalence of intersection point (udl 8.4)
studentTasks: explain why each yields same solution.
create a context matching given equations.
fadePlan: teacher models tri-rep connections. - gradually removes template supports. - students articulate independently across forms.
whenNotToUse: avoid if students already proficiently interconnect representations.
formativeChecks: - comparison chart check. - oral reasoning prompt: 'how do you know all forms agree?'

subject: math
name: community data projects
problemType: students see math as detached from real issues
targetMisconception: belief that math has no application to community improvement.
teacherMoves: introduce local data relevant to students’ community (udl 7.2)
guide question formulation about real-world issues (hlp inquiry)
model data analysis as civic reasoning (udl 8.4)
fadePlan: teacher models first local issue analysis → students plan group investigations with guidance → fade to independent, student-chosen projects.
whenNotToUse: avoid when curriculum pacing restricts open inquiry.
formativeChecks: - review research questions for relevance. - presentation peer feedback.

subject: math
name: critical data analysis and equity discussions
problemType: students interpret data without questioning bias
targetMisconception: belief that graphs and statistics are neutral.
teacherMoves: provide biased and unbiased data examples (udl 8.4)
facilitate discussion on representation and framing (hlp discourse)
prompt critique of missing voices (udl 7.3)
studentTasks: compare data sets for bias indicators.
fadePlan: teacher models bias identification → then supports small-group critiques → fade scaffolds as students independently identify bias.
whenNotToUse: avoid when lesson objective is purely computational.
formativeChecks: - exit slip: identify bias in new data. - group discussion notes.

subject: math
name: ethnomathematics connections
problemType: students think math was invented only by western cultures.
targetMisconception: belief that mathematical ideas belong to a single culture.
teacherMoves: share global mathematical contributions (udl 7.2)
facilitate research on cultural math practices (hlp inquiry)
discuss cultural influence on problem-solving methods (udl 8.3)
studentTasks: reflect on what remains relevant today.
fadePlan: teacher introduces exemplar cultures → groups research and present with minimal direction.
whenNotToUse: avoid in units requiring strict curriculum pacing.
formativeChecks: - evaluate depth of cultural connection. - peer feedback via rubric.

subject: math
name: quantitative social justice investigations
problemType: students fail to connect math with social issues.
targetMisconception: belief that numbers are neutral and apolitical.
teacherMoves: provide social issue datasets (udl 7.2)
model data interrogation and context framing (hlp inquiry)
facilitate dialogue on findings and implications (udl 8.4)
studentTasks: analyze data related to equity or sustainability.
fadePlan: teacher models analysis of one dataset → students conduct guided mini-inquiries → fade scaffolds to independent group projects.
whenNotToUse: avoid when class requires purely procedural review.
formativeChecks: - review reasoning in presentations. - reflection: “what story do the numbers tell?”

subject: math
name: mathematics in art and design
problemType: students fail to see creativity in math.
targetMisconception: belief that math and art are unrelated.
teacherMoves: show geometric art from diverse cultures (udl 7.3)
model pattern and symmetry analysis (hlp representation)
encourage student creation using math principles (udl 5.1)
fadePlan: teacher demonstrates initial example → students co-create designs → fade structure to open creative expression.
whenNotToUse: avoid when focus is algebraic fluency without conceptual linkage.
formativeChecks: - gallery walk peer feedback. - quick reflection: “where’s the math in my design?”

subject: math
name: mathematical storytelling circles
problemType: students disengage from abstract concept explanations.
targetMisconception: belief that storytelling is unrelated to mathematics.
teacherMoves: model mathematical storytelling (udl 7.3)
encourage oral and written math narratives (hlp discourse)
connect stories to problem-solving experiences (udl 6.4)
studentTasks: write or tell stories illustrating problem-solving journeys.
fadePlan: teacher models first math story → students co-create guided narratives → fade supports; students self-lead story circles.
whenNotToUse: avoid when time is limited or high content load.
formativeChecks: - evaluate clarity and math accuracy. - peer storytelling feedback.

subject: math
name: recontextualizing word problems for cultural relevance
problemType: word problems use unfamiliar cultural contexts.
targetMisconception: belief that only textbook examples count as 'real math'.
teacherMoves: replace textbook contexts with local examples (udl 7.2)
co-design problems with students (hlp co-design)
validate all community examples shared (udl 8.3)
studentTasks: identify culturally relevant contexts for target concepts.
rewrite sample problems with those contexts.
fadePlan: teacher models redesign of one example → students co-design under guidance → fade to student-initiated replacements.
whenNotToUse: avoid when uniform benchmark contexts are required by assessment.
formativeChecks: - review redesigned problems. - student feedback on relevance.

subject: math
name: student-created story problems
problemType: students view problems as teacher-generated only
targetMisconception: belief that personal experiences are irrelevant to math.
teacherMoves: model creation of story problems from daily contexts (udl 7.3)
highlight structure behind authentic scenarios (hlp modeling)
encourage multilingual drafts first (udl 2.1)
studentTasks: write math problems using personal or community contexts.
reflect on realism and math accuracy.
fadePlan: teacher co-creates first few examples → students author with scaffolds → fade to independent creation and translation.
whenNotToUse: avoid during high-stakes standardized review periods.
formativeChecks: - collect peer-review notes. - evaluate realism and math alignment.

subject: math
name: Culturally Sustaining Mathematics Practices
problemType: Mathematics curriculum excludes non-Western mathematical contributions and practices
targetMisconception: Belief that mathematics has only one history and one approach
teacherMoves: Include diverse mathematical traditions and contributions (UDL 7.3)
Teach mathematics as human cultural practice (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Connect to students' cultural mathematical knowledge (UDL 7.2)
Challenge Eurocentric narratives about mathematics (UDL 3.2)
studentTasks: Learn about diverse mathematical traditions and contributions
Connect mathematical concepts to cultural practices
Examine how culture shapes mathematical approaches
Bring own cultural mathematical knowledge to class
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher provides diverse mathematical history and validates traditions → Phase 2: Guided exploration of cultural connections → Phase 3: Student-led cultural math sharing → Phase 4: Ongoing culturally sustaining practice
whenNotToUse: When specific mathematical skill focus doesn't allow for cultural exploration time.

subject: math
name: Structured Argumentation Routines
problemType: Students struggle to critique reasoning constructively.
targetMisconception: Belief that disagreement is disrespectful.
teacherMoves: Teach “Claim-Evidence-Reasoning” routine (UDL 6.4)
Model respectful critique language (HLP Discourse)
Facilitate pair argument exchanges (UDL 8.3)
fadePlan: Teacher leads structured CERs first. • Students later lead peer critiques independently.
whenNotToUse: Avoid for rapid-fire recall activities.
formativeChecks: Evaluate use of evidence and tone. • Reflection log on feedback use.

subject: math
name: Establishing Equitable Discussion Norms
problemType: Some voices dominate class talk; others stay silent.
targetMisconception: Belief that math talk is only for students who know the answer.
teacherMoves: Co-create discussion norms emphasizing respect and wait time (UDL 8.3)
Model inviting quieter voices (HLP Discourse)
Reinforce idea contributions over correctness (UDL 9.3)
fadePlan: Teacher facilitates structured norm-building. • Students internalize and self-monitor equity. • Fade teacher prompts as norms sustain peer-to-peer.
whenNotToUse: Avoid during test review or independent work days.

subject: math
name: Group Roles and Accountability
problemType: Group work leads to unequal participation.
targetMisconception: Belief that collaboration means one person does the work.
teacherMoves: Define roles (recorder, facilitator, reporter) (UDL 8.3)
Rotate roles regularly (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Monitor accountability using checklists (UDL 6.3)
studentTasks: Assume rotating roles in group tasks.
fadePlan: Teacher enforces structured roles first. • Gradually removes checklists as students self-manage.
whenNotToUse: Avoid during brief pair-share interactions.
formativeChecks: Review checklists for equity. • Observe balanced participation.

subject: math
name: Math Talk Moves for Reasoning
problemType: Students give short answers without elaboration.
targetMisconception: Belief that explaining thinking is optional.
teacherMoves: Model talk moves (“revoice,” “press for reasoning”) (UDL 2.1)
Use sentence stems to scaffold explanations (HLP Discourse)
Provide positive feedback on elaboration (UDL 8.1)
studentTasks: Press for reasoning in small groups.
fadePlan: Teacher demonstrates talk moves. • Students practice in triads. • Fade stems as moves become spontaneous.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when class is focused on silent independent assessment.
formativeChecks: Observation checklist of reasoning statements. • Peer feedback notes.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Error Analysis and Learning
problemType: Students don't learn from mathematical errors
targetMisconception: Belief that errors are failures rather than learning opportunities
teacherMoves: Teach errors as valuable learning information (UDL 7.3)
Model productive error analysis (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice analyzing different error types (UDL 8.3)
Build error analysis habit (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Identify error type: conceptual, procedural, careless
Analyze what thinking led to error
Identify correct approach and why it works
Track error patterns for targeted improvement
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides error analysis explicitly → Phase 2: Structured error analysis with support → Phase 3: Independent error analysis → Phase 4: Automatic productive error response
whenNotToUse: When student is frustrated and needs support before analysis.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Error Analysis Protocol
problemType: Students repeat same errors without understanding why
targetMisconception: Belief that wrong answers are failures rather than learning opportunities
teacherMoves: Model analyzing worked examples with errors (UDL 3.2)
Categorize common error types (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Celebrate productive mistakes
studentTasks: Identify the specific error in worked problem
fadePlan: Teacher-provided errors → Partner error exchange → Self-error analysis
whenNotToUse: During initial concept introduction before students have attempts to analyze

subject: math
name: Estimation and Verification Routine
problemType: Students accept unreasonable answers without checking
targetMisconception: Belief that calculator answers are always correct
teacherMoves: Model estimation strategies before calculating (UDL 6.1)
Teach reasonableness checks (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice with deliberately wrong examples
studentTasks: Verify answer against estimate and context
fadePlan: Teacher models estimation thinking → Collaborative estimation → Independent habit
whenNotToUse: During pure procedural fluency practice

subject: math
name: Explicit Problem-Solving Steps Protocol
problemType: Students attempt problems without a systematic approach
targetMisconception: Belief that math talent means knowing answers instantly without process
teacherMoves: Model step-by-step think-aloud (UDL 6.1)
Name and post each problem-solving phase (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Provide worked examples with annotations
studentTasks: Follow posted steps for new problem
Annotate own thinking at each step
fadePlan: Full teacher modeling → Partial completion → Independent with checklist → Automaticity
whenNotToUse: When reviewing previously mastered procedures
formativeChecks: Exit ticket: Show all steps for one problem

subject: math
name: Home Language Mathematics Support
problemType: Multilingual students' home languages are underused in math
targetMisconception: Belief that math should be English-only
teacherMoves: Explicitly value multilingual assets in mathematics (UDL 7.3)
Allow home language for mathematical processing (UDL 5.3)
Provide bilingual math vocabulary support (UDL 3.1)
Connect to diverse mathematical traditions (UDL 7.3)
studentTasks: Use home language for mathematical thinking and processing
Make connections between languages for math concepts
Share mathematical thinking in preferred language
supports: Multilingual math processing permission and encouragement (UDL 7.3)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher explicitly encourages home language use → Phase 2: Structured translanguaging opportunities → Phase 3: Natural language use for math → Phase 4: Confident multilingual mathematical identity
whenNotToUse: Never - home language should always be valued in math. Adjust visibility as appropriate.

subject: math
name: graphical argument and counterargument
problemType: students state claims from graphs but do not justify
targetMisconception: belief that a visible trend is self-explanatory.
teacherMoves: model claim–evidence–reasoning with graph excerpts (udl 3.3)
provide counterclaim prompts (hlp explicit instruction)
facilitate rebuttal language practice (hlp discourse)
studentTasks: write a graph-based claim with cited evidence.
fadePlan: teacher-model cer → guided counterclaim drafting → independent rebuttal writing.
whenNotToUse: avoid when students have not learned to read graphs.
formativeChecks: - cer rubric check. - rebuttal clarity spot-check.

subject: math
name: using home language as an asset in math
problemType: els avoid participation in english-only discussions
targetMisconception: belief that math must be learned only in english.
teacherMoves: encourage translanguaging for idea generation (udl 2.1)
provide bilingual sentence stems for explanations (hlp cooperative learning)
model code-switching for precision (hlp language supports)
studentTasks: present final explanation in english with math vocabulary.
fadePlan: teacher-facilitated bilingual supports → peer-managed translation → independent choice of language supports.
whenNotToUse: avoid when translation resources are unavailable or confidentiality prohibits translation.
formativeChecks: - accuracy spot-check of translated terms. - peer feedback on clarity in final explanation.

subject: math
name: academic math vocabulary
problemType: students misuse or avoid math vocabulary
targetMisconception: belief that vocabulary is separate from reasoning.
teacherMoves: model precise vocabulary in context (udl 3.3)
provide morphology/cognate links (hlp language supports)
facilitate usage practice in pairs (hlp cooperative learning)
fadePlan: teacher modeling → guided pair work → independent usage logging.
whenNotToUse: avoid when conceptual understanding is still forming; pair with concept scaffold.
formativeChecks: - random usage check in explanations. - quick cognate/morphology quiz.

subject: math
name: sentence stems for reasoning
problemType: students struggle to express reasoning verbally
targetMisconception: belief that answers don’t require explanation.
teacherMoves: model academic stems for connectives (udl 5.3)
provide bank of reasoning stems (hlp language supports)
feedback on precision (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: replace stems with own phrasing over time.
fadePlan: teacher-modeled stems → guided with stems → independent phrasing.
whenNotToUse: avoid when the focus is pure computation check (no discussion time).
formativeChecks: - audit stem usage early. - check clarity/precision later.

subject: math
name: decoding and interpreting math symbols
problemType: students guess at symbols without meaning
targetMisconception: belief that symbols are arbitrary marks.
teacherMoves: model symbol decoding with examples/non-examples (udl 3.3)
provide symbol-to-meaning chart (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt translation to words (hlp language supports)
studentTasks: explain the symbol’s role in context.
fadePlan: teacher modeling → guided decoding → independent symbol translations.
whenNotToUse: avoid when the concept has not been introduced; preview concept first.
formativeChecks: - spot-check correct translation. - one-sentence symbol role explanation.

subject: math
name: from tables to expressions
problemType: students cannot translate tables into algebraic expressions
targetMisconception: belief that tables only show numbers, not structure.
teacherMoves: model recognizing patterns and writing expressions (udl 3.3)
highlight rate/initial value through think-aloud (hlp explicit instruction)
provide sentence frames for generalization (hlp language supports)
studentTasks: write expression for nth term or function rule.
justify the expression’s parts in words.
fadePlan: teacher models → guided pattern finding → independent generalization with stems removed.
whenNotToUse: avoid when tables are random or noisy without clear patterns.
formativeChecks: - mini-check: label which term is the rate vs. initial value. - quick explanation sentence linking table to expression.

subject: math
name: connecting manipulatives to symbolic notation
problemType: students use manipulatives without connecting to symbols
targetMisconception: belief that manipulatives are just toys or visuals.
teacherMoves: model mapping between manipulative actions and algebra steps (udl 3.3)
provide a side-by-side mapping chart (hlp representation)
prompt metacognitive “what does this step mean?” (hlp questioning)
studentTasks: explain meaning of each symbolic move.
fadePlan: teacher-led mapping → guided mapping → independent symbolic recording and meaning.
whenNotToUse: avoid if manipulatives are inaccessible or lesson is pure symbolic fluency.
formativeChecks: - collect mapping charts. - spot-check symbolic meaning sentences.

subject: math
name: visual proofs and reasoning
problemType: students memorize proofs without understanding
targetMisconception: belief that proof is only symbolic manipulation.
teacherMoves: model a visual proof (area/tiling) and narrate reasoning (udl 3.3)
provide structure prompts (claim–warrant–evidence) (hlp explicit instruction)
invite multiple perspectives on elegance/clarity (hlp discourse)
fadePlan: teacher-modeled visual proof → guided annotation → independent proof presentation.
whenNotToUse: avoid when time is too limited for discussion and critique.
formativeChecks: - rubric on clarity and correctness. - exit: one suggestion to improve a peer proof.

subject: math
name: interpreting graphs with visual language
problemType: students misread graphs and misinterpret trends
targetMisconception: believing graphs speak for themselves without analysis.
teacherMoves: model stepwise reading of graph axes, labels, and trends (udl 3.3)
provide annotated exemplar graphs (udl 1.1)
scaffold question stems for analysis (hlp explicit instruction)
fadePlan: teacher models analysis → guided practice with partial prompts → independent graph analysis.
whenNotToUse: avoid when graphs are too simple or students have mastered graph reading.

subject: math
name: translating word problems to math language
problemType: students copy numbers or miss relationships
targetMisconception: belief that every word maps one-to-one to symbols.
teacherMoves: model identifying quantities and relationships (udl 3.3)
provide translation frames (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt unit/relationship checks (hlp questioning)
fadePlan: teacher modeling → guided translation → independent with unit checks.
whenNotToUse: avoid when text complexity is too high; pre-teach vocabulary.
formativeChecks: - collect maps for a sample item. - one-sentence unit/relationship check.

subject: math
name: Math Anxiety Recognition and Management
problemType: Students experience anxiety that interferes with math performance
targetMisconception: Belief that anxiety means lack of math ability
teacherMoves: Normalize math anxiety and teach it's manageable (UDL 7.3)
Teach anxiety as physiological response (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Provide specific coping strategies for math contexts (UDL 6.4)
Create low-stakes practice opportunities (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Recognize personal math anxiety triggers and symptoms
Apply coping strategies before and during math
Create optimal conditions for math engagement
Build math confidence through success experiences
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides anxiety recognition and strategy introduction → Phase 2: Supported strategy practice → Phase 3: Independent anxiety management → Phase 4: Confident math engagement
whenNotToUse: When anxiety is severe enough to require professional support.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Argumentation and Justification
problemType: Students make claims without mathematical justification
targetMisconception: Belief that getting the right answer is sufficient without explanation
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical argumentation as core practice (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model constructing and critiquing arguments (UDL 6.1)
Practice justification using mathematical reasoning (UDL 8.3)
Build argumentation as habit (UDL 6.4)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models argumentation explicitly → Phase 2: Guided argumentation practice → Phase 3: Independent mathematical argument → Phase 4: Natural argumentation habits
whenNotToUse: When skill practice rather than justification is the goal.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Conjecture Making and Testing
problemType: Students don't engage in mathematical exploration through conjecture
targetMisconception: Belief that math is about following procedures not making discoveries
teacherMoves: Teach conjecture as mathematical practice (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model making and testing conjectures (UDL 6.1)
Practice systematic conjecture testing (UDL 8.3)
Build conjecture habit (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Make conjectures based on observations and patterns
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models conjecture process → Phase 2: Guided conjecture making and testing → Phase 3: Independent conjecture exploration → Phase 4: Natural conjecture habits
whenNotToUse: When verified procedures are being learned.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Discourse Community Building
problemType: Classroom doesn't function as mathematical learning community
targetMisconception: Belief that math class is about individual performance not community
teacherMoves: Establish mathematical discourse norms (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Model valuing all mathematical contributions (UDL 8.3)
Build on student thinking publicly (UDL 3.3)
Create culture where risk-taking is valued (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Take risks in sharing mathematical thinking
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher establishes norms and models community → Phase 2: Shared responsibility for community → Phase 3: Student-maintained community → Phase 4: Strong mathematical learning community
whenNotToUse: Never - mathematical community should be built continuously. Adjust approach based on needs.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Identity Affirmation and Development
problemType: Students don't see themselves as math capable
targetMisconception: Belief that some people are math people and others aren't
teacherMoves: Challenge fixed math ability beliefs explicitly (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Celebrate mathematical thinking not just answers (UDL 8.1)
Connect students to mathematicians who share identities (UDL 7.3)
Build success experiences that develop identity (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Challenge fixed ability beliefs with evidence
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher explicitly challenges beliefs and affirms → Phase 2: Supported identity exploration → Phase 3: Independent identity development → Phase 4: Strong mathematical identity
whenNotToUse: Never - mathematical identity should be developed continuously. Adjust intensity as needed.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Modeling Process Development
problemType: Students don't know how to model real situations mathematically
targetMisconception: Belief that math applies only to abstract problems
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical modeling as process (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model the full modeling cycle (UDL 6.1)
Practice with authentic modeling problems (UDL 7.2)
Build modeling skills progressively (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Identify situation to be modeled mathematically
Evaluate model and refine as needed
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models full cycle explicitly → Phase 2: Guided modeling with support → Phase 3: Independent modeling projects → Phase 4: Natural modeling approach
whenNotToUse: When routine problem-solving is the goal rather than modeling.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Persistence and Struggle Capacity
problemType: Students give up quickly on challenging problems
targetMisconception: Belief that not knowing immediately means inability
teacherMoves: Teach productive struggle as part of mathematical learning (UDL 7.3)
Model persistence with think-aloud during struggle (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Provide strategies for when stuck (UDL 6.4)
Celebrate persistence not just success (UDL 8.1)
studentTasks: Recognize struggle as normal part of learning
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher normalizes struggle with high support → Phase 2: Supported persistence with strategy cues → Phase 3: Independent persistence with reflection → Phase 4: Productive struggle identity
whenNotToUse: When struggle stems from missing prerequisite knowledge requiring reteaching.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Text Reading Comprehension
problemType: Students struggle to comprehend mathematical texts and problems
targetMisconception: Belief that reading math is the same as reading other texts
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical reading as specialized skill (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model reading mathematical text with think-aloud (UDL 6.1)
Practice decoding mathematical symbols and structures (UDL 3.2)
Build math reading fluency (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Read mathematical text for structure and meaning
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models math reading explicitly → Phase 2: Guided math reading practice → Phase 3: Independent math reading → Phase 4: Fluent mathematical reading
whenNotToUse: When mathematical content is presented verbally rather than in text.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Vocabulary Precision Development
problemType: Students use imprecise language that reflects or causes conceptual confusion
targetMisconception: Belief that mathematical vocabulary is unnecessary or interchangeable
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical vocabulary as precision tool (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model precise mathematical language (UDL 6.1)
Practice vocabulary in context of problem-solving (UDL 8.3)
Build vocabulary as ongoing practice (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Learn precise mathematical vocabulary for current content
Use vocabulary accurately in speaking and writing
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models and requires precise language → Phase 2: Prompted vocabulary use → Phase 3: Independent precise language → Phase 4: Natural mathematical precision
whenNotToUse: When exploring ideas and precision would inhibit thinking.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Writing Skill Development
problemType: Students can't write mathematically beyond showing calculations
targetMisconception: Belief that mathematics doesn't involve writing
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical writing as communication skill (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model different forms of mathematical writing (UDL 6.1)
Practice writing explanations, proofs, and reflections (UDL 8.3)
Build mathematical writing habits (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Use appropriate mathematical notation in writing
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models mathematical writing → Phase 2: Guided writing practice with feedback → Phase 3: Independent mathematical writing → Phase 4: Natural mathematical writing
whenNotToUse: When quick calculation is appropriate rather than written explanation.

subject: math
name: Multiple Representation Connector
problemType: Students use one representation without connecting to others
targetMisconception: Belief that graphs tables and equations are separate unrelated things
teacherMoves: Model translating between representations (UDL 3.3)
Highlight what each representation reveals (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Use color-coding across forms
studentTasks: Identify which representation best answers specific questions
fadePlan: Teacher models all connections → Students complete one representation given another → Independent multi-rep creation
whenNotToUse: When working on purely symbolic manipulation
formativeChecks: Explain why you chose specific representation

subject: math
name: Multiple Representations Fluency Building
problemType: Students get stuck in one representation when others might help
targetMisconception: Belief that there's one right way to represent mathematical ideas
teacherMoves: Teach multiple representations as fundamental mathematical skill (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model translating between representations (UDL 5.1)
Practice choosing representations strategically (UDL 7.1)
Build fluency in moving between representations (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Represent problems using multiple forms: verbal, symbolic, graphical, tabular
Choose representations strategically for different purposes
Use multiple representations to verify solutions
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models with explicit translation → Phase 2: Guided representation practice → Phase 3: Independent representation choice → Phase 4: Natural representation fluency
whenNotToUse: When specific representation practice is the learning goal.

subject: math
name: attention signaling routines (exec function)
problemType: students miss instructions or forget multi-part directions
targetMisconception: belief that attention automatically follows spoken instruction.
teacherMoves: establish consistent visual/auditory attention cues (udl 7.3)
model stop-look-listen and chunked directives (hlp explicit instruction)
provide written anchor for steps (udl 6.3)
studentTasks: check off steps as they are completed.
fadePlan: teacher-led cues with explicit modeling → guided cue-response with paraphrase → independent attention/self-cueing.
whenNotToUse: avoid when students are in crisis or sensory overload; use calmer routine first.
formativeChecks: - quick check: students paraphrase directions accurately. - observation: response time to cues.

subject: math
name: executive function checklist
problemType: students forget materials, steps, or goals across a lesson
targetMisconception: belief that organization is purely willpower.
teacherMoves: co-create checklist for materials/steps/goals (udl 6.3)
model self-check routine (hlp explicit instruction)
celebrate consistent use (hlp feedback)
fadePlan: teacher-created lists → co-created → student-generated and self-managed.
whenNotToUse: avoid during high-stakes assessment segments where checklists aren’t permitted.
formativeChecks: - checklist completion rates. - weekly ef reflection entry.

subject: math
name: retrieval practice routines
problemType: students reread notes instead of retrieving
targetMisconception: belief that learning equals re-reading.
teacherMoves: teach short, spaced retrieval cycles (udl 6.4)
model self-quiz design (hlp explicit instruction)
provide error log and fix-up strategies (hlp feedback)
fadePlan: teacher-led retrieval sessions → guided self-quiz design → independent spaced retrieval.
whenNotToUse: avoid cramming situations that demand new content, not recall.
formativeChecks: - error log improvements over time. - spot check self-quiz quality.

subject: math
name: multisensory instruction pack
problemType: students benefit from visual, auditory, and kinesthetic inputs
targetMisconception: belief that one modality fits all learners.
teacherMoves: model concept with visual, verbal, and tactile elements (udl 1.1/2.1/3.1)
provide choice of input modality (udl 7.2)
coach students to choose and reflect (hlp self-regulation)
studentTasks: try at least two modalities for a concept.
fadePlan: teacher-curated multisensory demo → student choice with guidance → independent modality selection.
whenNotToUse: avoid when environment or materials limit modality access.
formativeChecks: - reflection: which modality supported understanding and why? - peer explanation in chosen modality.

subject: math
name: processing speed scaffold
problemType: students rush or stall on long items without strategy
targetMisconception: belief that pacing is innate and cannot be adjusted.
teacherMoves: model timeboxing for sub-steps (udl 6.3)
provide “good-enough now, refine later” heuristic (hlp explicit instruction)
coach peer-timed practice (hlp cooperative learning)
fadePlan: teacher-led timeboxing → guided peer timing → independent self-pacing.
whenNotToUse: avoid during summative testing with fixed timing rules.
formativeChecks: - compare planned vs. actual times. - reflection on one pacing adjustment.

subject: math
name: structured note systems
problemType: students’ notes are incomplete or unusable for studying
targetMisconception: belief that good notes mean copying everything.
teacherMoves: model cornell/structure-first notes (udl 6.3)
provide cue columns and summary prompts (hlp explicit instruction)
teach weekly “tidy + reflect” routine (hlp feedback)
fadePlan: teacher-modeled structure → guided notes with prompts → independent structured notes.
whenNotToUse: avoid for very short tasks where note-taking is unnecessary.
formativeChecks: - random spot-check for summary accuracy. - reflection on how notes improved recall.

subject: math
name: visual sequence maps
problemType: students lose track of procedure order or skip steps
targetMisconception: belief that steps are arbitrary and order doesn’t matter.
teacherMoves: model flowchart mapping of multi-step procedures (udl 5.1)
color-code decision points (udl 2.5)
prompt “why this step now?” (hlp questioning)
studentTasks: build a flowchart for a target procedure.
fadePlan: teacher-created flowcharts → guided additions → student-created flowcharts.
whenNotToUse: avoid when the task genuinely has flexible order (focus on strategy selection instead).
formativeChecks: - flowchart completeness/accuracy check. - one-sentence step justification.

subject: math
name: chunking multi-step problems (exec function)
problemType: students lose procedural steps or fail to monitor progress
targetMisconception: belief that long problems must be solved in one go.
teacherMoves: model chunk–check routine with timers (udl 6.3)
provide visual step planner (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt self-talk for next-step planning (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: break a long problem into chunks.
set a goal per chunk and monitor completion.
reflect on which chunk needed a strategy.
fadePlan: teacher-led chunking → guided chunk-and-check → independent chunking with self-monitor.
whenNotToUse: avoid when problems are intentionally short/one-step practice.
formativeChecks: - planner completeness check. - reflections cite one chunk and strategy used.

subject: math
name: Pattern Recognition and Generalization Skills
problemType: Students don't recognize or generalize mathematical patterns
targetMisconception: Belief that each math problem is unique rather than connected by patterns
teacherMoves: Teach pattern recognition as mathematical practice (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model identifying and extending patterns (UDL 6.1)
Practice generalizing from specific cases (UDL 6.2)
Connect patterns to formal mathematical concepts (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Generalize patterns into mathematical rules or formulas
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models pattern recognition and generalization → Phase 2: Guided pattern work → Phase 3: Independent pattern recognition → Phase 4: Natural pattern-seeking habits
whenNotToUse: When specific procedural fluency is the goal.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Peer Explanation and Teaching
problemType: Students don't learn from explaining to or teaching peers
targetMisconception: Belief that explaining to others takes time away from own learning
teacherMoves: Teach peer explanation as learning tool for explainer (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Model effective mathematical explanations (UDL 6.1)
Structure peer teaching opportunities (UDL 8.3)
Build explanation skills progressively (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Prepare to explain mathematical concepts to peers
Explain using multiple representations and examples
Check peer understanding and adjust explanation
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models explanations with structure → Phase 2: Supported peer teaching → Phase 3: Independent peer explanation → Phase 4: Natural peer teaching culture
whenNotToUse: When content is new to everyone and peer teaching isn't appropriate.

subject: math
name: Problem Understanding and Entry Protocol
problemType: Students start calculating before understanding problems
targetMisconception: Belief that math is about quickly finding answers rather than understanding
teacherMoves: Teach problem understanding as essential first step (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model reading problems multiple times (UDL 6.1)
Practice identifying what's given and what's asked (UDL 6.2)
Build habit of pausing before solving (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Read problem multiple times for understanding
Identify what's given and what's being asked
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models understanding protocol explicitly → Phase 2: Prompted understanding before solving → Phase 3: Independent understanding protocol → Phase 4: Automatic understanding habit
whenNotToUse: When problem is routine and understanding is already automatic.

subject: math
name: applying exponent rules (fluency)
problemType: students memorize rules without understanding
targetMisconception: belief that rules are arbitrary patterns.
teacherMoves: connect rules to repeated multiplication visuals (udl 3.3)
contrast similar-looking rules with examples/non-examples (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt verbalization of rule meaning (hlp language supports)
studentTasks: complete contrast sets (e.g., product vs. power rules).
repair a wrong application in a sample.
fadePlan: full modeling. • guided contrasts. • independent practice with repair tasks.
whenNotToUse: avoid when exponential meaning has not been introduced conceptually.
formativeChecks: - quick fix-a-rule item. - one explanation sentence per problem.

subject: math
name: factoring quadratics fluency
problemType: students memorize patterns without structural understanding
targetMisconception: belief that factoring is trial-and-error only.
teacherMoves: model structure-first factor recognition (udl 3.3)
color-code factor pairs (udl 2.5)
prompt articulation of why factors produce terms (hlp explicit instruction)
fadePlan: teacher-led modeling. - guided sort and factor. - independent factoring with explanation.
whenNotToUse: avoid when concept is new (teach conceptual scaffold first).
formativeChecks: - exit: justify factor choice on one problem. - self-check expansion matches original.

subject: math
name: operations with fractions (fluency)
problemType: students rely on calculators or avoid fraction operations
targetMisconception: belief that fraction operations are arbitrary tricks.
teacherMoves: model common denominator reasoning (udl 3.3)
verbalize numerator/denominator roles (hlp explicit instruction)
provide error analysis mini-sets (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: complete practice sets emphasizing structure and error correction.
reflect on a frequent error and a fix.
fadePlan: full modeling. - guided sets with trackers. - independent sets with self-correction.
whenNotToUse: avoid when the focus is conceptual understanding (use conceptual scaffold first).
formativeChecks: - mini-quiz with two error items to repair. - pair explanation spot-checks.

subject: math
name: stepwise solving linear equations
problemType: procedural fluency without reasoning about inverse operations
targetMisconception: belief that solving is just crossing out.
teacherMoves: model inverse operations while verbalizing balance reasoning (udl 3.3)
write and highlight each transformation step (udl 6.3)
prompt partner explanation for each step (hlp peer collaboration)
studentTasks: solve curated problems and check balance after each step.
fadePlan: teacher-led worked examples. - fade to guided practice with trackers. - independent solving with self-check.
whenNotToUse: avoid when focus is conceptual exploration (use conceptual scaffold instead).
formativeChecks: - spot-check partner explanations for correctness. - quick exit: identify which step preserved balance.

subject: math
name: transformations between linear forms
problemType: students convert forms without understanding structure
targetMisconception: belief that form changes are arbitrary.
teacherMoves: model converting between slope-intercept and standard form with structure notes (udl 3.3)
provide align/transform checklist (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt explanation of parameter effects (hlp questioning)
fadePlan: teacher modeling. • guided transform with notes. • independent transforms with explanation.
whenNotToUse: avoid before students can read graphs/parameters.
formativeChecks: - spot-check structure notes. - one-sentence parameter-effect reasoning.

subject: math
name: simplifying radicals (fluency)
problemType: students treat radicals like integers
targetMisconception: belief that √(a+b) = √a + √b.
teacherMoves: model structure and counterexamples (udl 3.3)
provide prime factor tree technique (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt “why valid?” checks (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: write a note on why simplification is valid.
fadePlan: teacher-led examples. • guided practice with trackers. • independent sets.
whenNotToUse: avoid when square roots are brand new (teach concept first).
formativeChecks: - quick counterexample identification. - exit: explain why √(a+b) ≠ √a+√b.

subject: math
name: fluency with slope-intercept form
problemType: students memorize y=mx+b steps but can’t apply flexibly
targetMisconception: belief that slope-intercept works the same in any context.
teacherMoves: model identifying slope and intercepts from multiple representations (udl 3.3)
provide quick transforms to/from standard form (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt explanation of how parameters change graphs (hlp questioning)
studentTasks: extract m and b from graphs/tables.
explain graph changes for parameter tweaks.
fadePlan: teacher modeling. - guided transform practice. - independent parameter reasoning.
whenNotToUse: avoid when lesson focus is conceptual rate meaning (use conceptual scaffold).
formativeChecks: - quick transform check. - one-sentence reasoning of parameter change.

subject: math
name: elimination method fluency
problemType: students add equations without aligning terms or understanding why it works
targetMisconception: belief that elimination is a trick unrelated to substitution.
teacherMoves: model term alignment and multiplying by constants (udl 3.3)
think-aloud justification of elimination step (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt “why this combination” reflections (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: align terms, choose multipliers, eliminate and solve.
explain why the step preserves equality.
compare with substitution on one example.
fadePlan: teacher-led demonstration. - guided practice with template. - independent elimination with justification.
whenNotToUse: avoid when conceptual connections among methods haven’t been introduced.
formativeChecks: - spot-check justification sentences. - quick compare/contrast note vs substitution.

subject: math
name: Real-World Mathematics Connection Building
problemType: Students don't see relevance of mathematics to their lives
targetMisconception: Belief that math is abstract and disconnected from reality
teacherMoves: Connect mathematical content to real applications (UDL 7.2)
Use authentic problems from student contexts (UDL 7.2)
Explore careers using mathematics (UDL 7.3)
Support student-identified connections (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Identify real-world applications of concepts being learned
Explore mathematics in areas of personal interest
Research careers that use current mathematical content
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher provides connections and guides exploration → Phase 2: Supported connection discovery → Phase 3: Independent relevance finding → Phase 4: Natural math-world connections
whenNotToUse: When abstract mathematical development is appropriate learning goal.

subject: math
name: error analysis for reasoning
problemType: students see errors as failure not feedback
targetMisconception: belief that correctness is the only measure.
teacherMoves: model categorizing and repairing errors (udl 3.3)
facilitate debate on borderline cases (hlp discourse)
prompt “what changed your mind?” (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: classify and repair errors with explanations.
write a reflection on a repaired misconception.
fadePlan: teacher-led classification → guided repair → independent error analysis.
whenNotToUse: avoid when current unit is foundational and time is short.
formativeChecks: - mini-rubric on justification quality. - reflection cites one misconception repair.

subject: math
name: developing estimation sense
problemType: students rely solely on exact calculation
targetMisconception: belief that estimation is guessing.
teacherMoves: model front-end and rounding strategies (udl 3.3)
provide estimation checkpoints (hlp explicit instruction)
prompt reasonableness reflection (hlp feedback)
studentTasks: reflect on error size and method.
fadePlan: teacher modeling. • guided estimation with checkpoints. • independent estimation use.
whenNotToUse: avoid when exact computation is the explicit objective.
formativeChecks: - exit: compare/justify estimate vs exact on one item. - reflection on best-fit strategy.

subject: math
name: metacognitive reflection in math
problemType: students don’t connect strategy to outcome
targetMisconception: belief that success/failure is random.
teacherMoves: model brief reflection after tasks (udl 6.4)
provide question stems linking strategy→result (hlp explicit instruction)
encourage peer share of strategies (hlp cooperative learning)
studentTasks: identify which strategy helped and why.
share one strategy in peer group.
fadePlan: teacher-modeled reflections → guided entries → independent reflections.
whenNotToUse: avoid when time is too short to write (consider oral reflection).
formativeChecks: - review reflections for strategy–result link. - peer share quality spot-check.

subject: math
name: modeling real-world contexts
problemType: students compute without interpreting parameters
targetMisconception: belief that models are just equations unrelated to context.
teacherMoves: model interpreting parameters in context (udl 3.3)
provide structure notes for assumptions/limits (hlp explicit instruction)
facilitate peer critique of model choices (hlp discourse)
studentTasks: fit a model to a context.
fadePlan: teacher-led modeling → guided interpretation/limits → independent modeling + critique.
whenNotToUse: avoid when context knowledge is missing; preview context first.
formativeChecks: - check parameter interpretations. - critique notes quality.

subject: math
name: exploring multiple strategies
problemType: students stick to one procedure even when inefficient
targetMisconception: belief that there is only one right way.
teacherMoves: model alternative strategies on one task (udl 3.3)
facilitate compare/contrast discussion (hlp discourse)
prompt metacognitive choice of strategy (hlp self-regulation)
studentTasks: solve a task using two strategies.
justify choice of strategy next time.
fadePlan: teacher-led exploration → guided compare/contrast → independent strategy choice.
whenNotToUse: avoid when time is only for fluency drills.
formativeChecks: - quick compare/contrast note. - reflection on chosen strategy.

subject: math
name: engaging with open-ended tasks
problemType: students avoid non-routine tasks
targetMisconception: belief that tasks must have one right path.
teacherMoves: model multiple entry points and success criteria (udl 3.3)
provide low-floor/high-ceiling prompts (hlp inquiry)
facilitate share-explain-compare routine (hlp discourse)
studentTasks: tackle open tasks with a chosen entry point.
explain approach and compare with peers.
fadePlan: teacher-led entry-point modeling → guided sharing → independent open-task work.
whenNotToUse: avoid when objective is timed fluency only.
formativeChecks: - collect solution comparisons. - reflection on flexibility.

subject: math
name: decomposing complex problems
problemType: students attempt problems as a single block
targetMisconception: belief that all steps must be discovered at once.
teacherMoves: model problem decomposition with sub-goals (udl 3.3)
provide sub-goal template (hlp explicit instruction)
coach monitor-and-adjust (hlp feedback)
fadePlan: teacher-modeled decomposition → guided sub-goals → independent decomposition.
whenNotToUse: avoid when the target is a short, single-step task.
formativeChecks: - sub-goal plan quality check. - one adjustment justified.

subject: math
name: constructing mathematical arguments
problemType: students assert without justification
targetMisconception: belief that a claim stands without evidence.
teacherMoves: model claim–evidence–reasoning in math context (udl 3.3)
provide justification frames (hlp explicit instruction)
facilitate rebuttal routine (hlp discourse)
fadePlan: teacher-modeled arguments → guided frames → independent arguments.
whenNotToUse: avoid when formal proof language has not been introduced.
formativeChecks: - argument rubric check. - one defended rebuttal required.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Self-Monitoring for Accuracy
problemType: Students don't check work or recognize unreasonable answers
targetMisconception: Belief that first answer is final answer
teacherMoves: Teach self-monitoring as essential math practice (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model checking strategies (UDL 6.1)
Practice catching common error types (UDL 8.3)
Build checking habit (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Identify and correct errors before submitting
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher prompts checking at each step → Phase 2: Self-prompted checking with support → Phase 3: Independent monitoring habit → Phase 4: Automatic checking behavior
whenNotToUse: When time pressure prevents thorough checking (adapt to quick checks).

subject: math
name: Mathematics for Social Justice Applications
problemType: Students don't see mathematics as tool for understanding and addressing injustice
targetMisconception: Belief that mathematics is neutral and disconnected from social issues
teacherMoves: Connect mathematical analysis to social justice issues (UDL 7.2)
Use authentic data about equity issues (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Support critical mathematical analysis (UDL 3.2)
Move from analysis to potential action (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Use mathematics to analyze social justice issues
Apply statistical and quantitative reasoning to equity data
Critique uses and misuses of mathematics
Consider action based on mathematical analysis
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher provides issues and guides analysis → Phase 2: Supported issue exploration → Phase 3: Independent social justice math → Phase 4: Critical mathematical citizenship
whenNotToUse: When mathematical skill building is the primary focus.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Solution Process Communication
problemType: Students show final answers without explaining reasoning
targetMisconception: Belief that math is about getting right answers not explaining thinking
teacherMoves: Teach mathematical communication as essential skill (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model explaining reasoning with think-aloud (UDL 6.1)
Practice writing mathematical explanations (UDL 5.3)
Build habit of justifying steps (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Show all work with logical organization
Explain why each step makes sense mathematically
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models explicit explanation → Phase 2: Guided explanation practice → Phase 3: Independent solution communication → Phase 4: Natural mathematical communication
whenNotToUse: When speed is prioritized over explanation (timed assessments).

subject: math
name: Problem-Solving Strategy Selection Metacognition
problemType: Students use same approach for all problems regardless of type
targetMisconception: Belief that there's one way to solve math problems
teacherMoves: Teach strategic thinking about problem-solving approaches (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model strategy selection with rationale (UDL 6.1)
Practice matching strategies to problem types (UDL 6.2)
Build strategic flexibility (UDL 7.1)
studentTasks: Reflect on strategy choice and adjust for future
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models strategy selection with thinking → Phase 2: Guided strategy selection with feedback → Phase 3: Independent strategic thinking → Phase 4: Natural strategic flexibility
whenNotToUse: When specific strategy practice is the learning goal.

subject: math
name: Mathematical Technology Tool Integration
problemType: Students don't know how to use technology effectively for math
targetMisconception: Belief that technology does the thinking rather than supporting it
teacherMoves: Teach strategic technology use for mathematics (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model when and how to use different tools (UDL 5.2)
